name: Chavez
label: Matador
lede: Chavez made two records for Matador, got a spin on Beavis and Butt-Head, and never officially broke up. They just wandered off to play with Johnny Cash, write for HBO and direct movies, and the records stayed in circulation among guitar players.

eras.title: Wider's leftovers, a Harvard guy and a Hollywood kid
eras.text: Chavez grew out of the New York band Wider in 1993. The line-up: a New Jersey guitarist who'd made records as a teenager, a Harvard graduate from a Boston hard rock band, and the son of the man who made Happy Days.

years.cap: Chavez: Clay Tarver, Matt Sweeney, James Lo and Scott Marshall
years.src: Wikipedia: Chavez · Wikipedia: Matt Sweeney · Wikipedia: Clay Tarver · Wikipedia: Scott Marshall
years.h: Two Wider alumni, a Bullet LaVolta guitarist and Garry Marshall's son
years.p: [[Matt Sweeney|256a32b5-7ba5-4560-bf1f-2632628a7e53]] and drummer James Lo leave Wider and start Chavez in New York with guitarist [[Clay Tarver|7137b936-0210-478d-b9ff-f02c2aef8863]] and bassist [[Scott Marshall|ffcc505e-5b7d-4ac3-b333-11f6c8dcd401]].
years.xp:
Sweeney, raised in Maplewood and South Orange, New Jersey, had already made two records on Twin/Tone with his high-school band Skunk. Tarver, born in San Antonio and a 1988 Harvard graduate, had co-led the Boston band [[Bullet LaVolta|7913528c-6263-41c1-b488-aeae8fc291a9]], which recorded for Taang!, RCA and Matador before splitting in 1991.

Marshall is the son of director Garry Marshall and nephew of Penny Marshall. Sweeney has described the aim as the Jesus Lizard with more melodies: "all that tough angular stuff."

years.h: The first single, Repeat the Ending, builds a following in New York
years.p: Repeat the Ending puts Chavez on the New York underground's radar before they have an album.

years.h: Gone Glimmering gets made on weekends
years.p: Chavez records its debut over weekends in December 1994 and January 1995, with [[Bob Weston|7364260a-0a3e-4a6c-bcf8-b4e743c0b2c0]], Bryce Goggin and John Agnello producing alongside the band.

eras.title: Two Matador records and a Beavis and Butt-Head moment
eras.text: Everything most fans know came out in eighteen months. The riffs were angular and lopsided, the dynamics dropped out from under you, and critics reached for The Jesus Lizard, Blue Öyster Cult and Cheap Trick.

q: No debut of late combines guts and gray matter quite as fluently.
years.h: Gone Glimmering opens with Nailed to the Blank Spot
years.p: Matador releases the debut: nine songs, about 30 minutes. Billboard says no recent debut combines guts and gray matter so fluently.
years.xp:
The album runs from Nailed to the Blank Spot to Relaxed Fit, with Break Up Your Band second and Pentagram Ring fifth. The Albuquerque Tribune called it "a big load of rock, pounded with a New York Noise mallet."

The bassist is credited as Scott Anthony Masciarelli, his family's original surname; his father Garry Marshall was born Masciarelli.

years.h: Beavis and Butt-Head watch Break Up Your Band
years.p: MTV's Beavis and Butt-Head airs the video for Break Up Your Band, the second song on Gone Glimmering.

years.h: The Pentagram Ring EP follows within the year
years.p: Chavez follows Gone Glimmering with an EP named for the album's fifth song, Pentagram Ring.

years.h: Chavez goes on the road with Guided by Voices and Bardo Pond
years.p: Chavez tours with [[Guided by Voices|6c85f4c3-026c-4c16-9a7c-f546f42ed0fb]] and [[Bardo Pond|2ad8bce1-8e55-48db-82ed-d98b52a3a13f]], and Sweeney fills in on bass for Guided by Voices' Under the Bushes Under the Stars tour.

q: A fine specimen of spare, brainy post-metal hard rock.
years.h: Ride the Fader is the second and last album
years.p: Matador releases the follow-up, co-produced with John Agnello and Bryce Goggin. Entertainment Weekly gives it an A.
years.xp:
Twelve songs in 38 minutes, from Top Pocket Man to You Must Be Stopped, with Unreal Is Here third and Flight '96 the longest at 5:30. Fans and critics tend to call it the band's best.

Not everyone agreed: NME gave it 5 out of 10.

eras.title: Not broken up, just busy
eras.text: Chavez toured the US and Europe through 1997, then went quiet: few shows, no new music between 1999 and 2006. They never split. The members were busy elsewhere.

years.h: Eight years, a handful of shows, no breakup
years.p: From 1999 to 2006 Chavez releases nothing and plays only a few shows. According to Wikipedia, the band never officially broke up.

Matt Sweeney forms [[Zwan|5af2629b-36de-486c-ad50-a89a28ff050f]] with [[Billy Corgan|3cbfd3e3-6d9b-4327-84ba-42cf646c98f9]] and [[Jimmy Chamberlin|48d3d17b-0bb8-44a0-9fb0-23f594bb4df3]] of the [[Smashing Pumpkins|ba0d6274-db14-4ef5-b28d-657ebde1a396]]; [[David Pajo|85188c46-d3ed-4517-ba78-5d06ec764f1c]] of [[Slint|2869c510-2679-4a3f-bf15-e5e8b49f2f28]] is in the line-up too.

years.h: Tarver writes a thriller with J.J. Abrams
years.p: Clay Tarver, who also made the Jimmy the Cabdriver interstitials for MTV, co-writes Joy Ride with J.J. Abrams.

years.h: Sweeney and Will Oldham release Superwolf
years.p: Matt Sweeney and [[Will Oldham|eb51090c-662a-47a1-967c-c63292d9831a]] put out Superwolf. He also plays guitar on Rick Rubin's Johnny Cash sessions, heard on American V (2006) and American VI (2010).

eras.title: Better days, bigger day jobs
eras.text: Matador gathered almost everything Chavez ever recorded onto one compilation in 2006, and the band started playing again, with shows alongside Pavement and Sonic Youth and a slot at All Tomorrow's Parties. The members' day jobs got bigger too.

years.h: Better Days Will Haunt You brings Chavez back to the stage
years.p: Matador's compilation collects virtually all of Chavez's studio recordings, with new vocals on White Jeans. The band starts playing select shows again.
years.xp: After the compilation the band played shows with [[Pavement|36bfa85f-737b-41db-a8fc-b8825850ffc3]] and [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]].

years.h: Scott Marshall directs Keeping Up with the Steins
years.p: The AFI-trained bassist directs the comedy Keeping Up with the Steins, then Blonde Ambition in 2007.

years.cap: Chavez at Matador's 21st-anniversary party, Las Vegas
years.h: Chavez plays All Tomorrow's Parties in Asbury Park
years.p: Chavez is on the bill of ATP I'll Be Your Mirror in Asbury Park, New Jersey, in September 2011. In May 2012 they play the London edition at Alexandra Palace.

years.h: Sweeney asks famous guitarists how they do it
years.p: His web series Guitar Moves, where well-known players show how they play, launches on Vice's Noisey channel.

yt: Tarver interview: Bullet LaVolta, Silicon Valley
years.h: Tarver wins a Writers Guild award for Silicon Valley
years.p: Tarver, later co-showrunner of HBO's Silicon Valley, wins the Writers Guild award for Episodic Comedy for Sand Hill Shuffle. Sweeney tours with [[Iggy Pop|f37b3f31-b1f8-4b88-8cb5-b34f709b17d7]] that year.

years.h: Cockfighters, the first new Chavez since 1996
years.p: The Cockfighters EP is Chavez's first new record since Ride the Fader.

years.h: Sweeney and Stephen Malkmus start The Hard Quartet
years.p: Sweeney forms [[The Hard Quartet|bc67223b-b2b5-4431-92e6-620651978c6c]] with [[Stephen Malkmus|eaefd603-84c1-4db4-a72b-0cb718a0cc07]] of [[Pavement|36bfa85f-737b-41db-a8fc-b8825850ffc3]], [[Jim White|e1f83b22-d40e-400a-8ebb-4e59b5b53d31]] and Emmett Kelly; they tour the world in 2025.
